data.title: B1 Progress Check
data.description: A second mixed grammar check to measure progress and confirm whether the learner is working securely at CEFR B1 level.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using the present perfect.
sections.explain: Use 'have/has' + past participle with 'yet' in negative sentences and questions. The correct form is 'hasn't finished yet'.

words.word: She hasn't finished her homework yet.
She didn't finish her homework yet.
She hasn't finish her homework yet.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct first conditional sentence.
sections.explain: Use the present simple after 'if' and 'will' + base verb in the main clause for a real future possibility.

words.word: If you leave now, you will catch the train.
If you will leave now, you will catch the train.
If you leave now, you will caught the train.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence for an unreal present situation.
sections.explain: Use 'if' + past simple and 'would' + base verb for an unreal or unlikely present situation.

words.word: If I were you, I would speak to the manager.
If I would be you, I spoke to the manager.
If I am you, I would speak to the manager.

sections.explain: In reported questions, use statement word order and do not use 'do' or 'did'. The correct form is 'asked me where I lived'.

words.word: He asked me where I lived.
He asked me where did I live.
He asked me where I did live.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct defining relative clause.
sections.explain: Use 'that' or 'which' to introduce a defining relative clause about a thing. Do not repeat the object pronoun.

words.word: This is the book that I told you about.
This is the book that I told you about it.
This is the book who I told you about.

sections.explain: The present simple passive is formed with 'am/is/are' + past participle. The correct form is 'is spoken'.

words.word: English is spoken in many countries.
English speaks in many countries.
English is speak in many countries.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct modal expression of possibility.
sections.explain: Use 'might' + base verb to express possibility. The correct form is 'might arrive'.

words.word: They might arrive later this evening.
They might to arrive later this evening.
They might arriving later this evening.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct verb pattern after 'enjoy'.
sections.explain: The verb 'enjoy' is followed by the -ing form. The correct structure is 'enjoy reading'.

words.word: I really enjoy reading historical novels.
I really enjoy to read historical novels.
I really enjoy read historical novels.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using the past perfect.
sections.explain: Use the past perfect for an action completed before another past action. The correct form is 'had left'.

words.word: By the time we arrived, the train had left.
By the time we arrived, the train has left.
By the time we arrived, the train left already.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct sentence showing a past habit.
sections.explain: Use 'used to' + base verb for a past habit or state that is no longer true.

words.word: I used to play tennis every weekend.
I use to play tennis every weekend.
I used to playing tennis every weekend.
